name: NeuralPath PayNode Subdermal Transaction Implant
body_location: subdermal hand — dorsal surface, between metacarpals of index and middle finger
description:
The PayNode is a subdermal near-field transaction chip implanted in the dorsal hand, positioned to sit within 15mm of the skin surface for reliable near-field communication at standard payment terminals. The core unit is a passive NFC/biometric authentication module approximately the size of a grain of rice, paired with a slightly larger cryptographic co-processor node that handles transaction signing and security. Unlike legacy external payment devices, the PayNode authenticates via the user's unique biometric pulse signature — a combination of vascular geometry and micro-electrical skin conductance — meaning the chip cannot be used by anyone else even if somehow extracted. It supports all standard Quanta-denominated civic financial protocols, interfaces with municipal transit systems, access control networks, vending infrastructure, and peer-to-peer transfers. A linked app or BCI interface displays balance and transaction history, though the implant functions entirely offline for standard tap payments.

The PayNode is arguably the single most installed piece of cyberware in GLMZ after civic identity chips — in many Tier 1 and Tier 2 neighborhoods, cash infrastructure has deteriorated to the point where a physical wallet is useless, and external payment devices are easily stolen. Having your money literally in your hand is not a metaphor; it is a practical security consideration for anyone living in areas where muggings are common. Children in Tier 2 households often receive their first PayNode around age ten, loaded with a supervised allowance account. The gesture of payment — a casual wave of the hand over a terminal, no pause, no pocket-reaching — has become so normalized that older residents who remember external devices describe the transition as roughly equivalent to the shift from cash to cards two centuries prior.
installation_requirements: Pharmacy kiosk installation; 10-minute procedure, topical anesthetic only, no recovery time; biometric enrollment completed at installation
maintenance: No battery (passive NFC, terminal-powered); cryptographic key rotation recommended annually via certified NeuralPath terminal; physical node is rated for 15-year service life before optional replacement

side_effects: Faint warmth in the hand during high-value transactions while cryptographic signing processes
Mild swelling at installation site for 3–5 days post-procedure
Occasional false-read rejections at poorly maintained terminals, requiring a second tap
Some users report a subtle awareness of the node when hands are very cold, described as a faint pressure
cultural_context: The PayNode is culturally invisible in most of GLMZ — it is so standard that noticing someone use it is like noticing someone breathe. The hand-wave payment gesture has become a social norm so embedded that it appears in children's play, casual mimicry, and even as a shorthand gesture meaning 'I'll cover it' among friends. In Tier 1 communities, it carries a faint class marker in the opposite direction from most tech: not having one suggests extreme poverty or deliberate off-grid living, both of which carry their own social weight. There is a small but active community of privacy advocates who refuse PayNode implants on surveillance grounds, preferring anonymous physical currency — a stance that makes daily life in most of GLMZ genuinely inconvenient. Criminals who target PayNode users typically focus on coerced authentication rather than physical extraction, which has driven a secondary market in panic-code features that silently alert civic services while completing a transaction.
known_users: children from age 8-10 onward in most families
street vendors and informal economy workers
anyone living in areas where carrying external valuables is dangerous
story_hooks: A series of payments are being made on a dead woman's PayNode — biometric authentication should make this impossible, yet the transactions are clearing, suggesting someone has found a way to spoof the vascular signature or the node was removed and is being kept viable somehow

A Tier 1 neighborhood's entire PayNode population received an unauthorized firmware push overnight — nobody knows who sent it or what it changed, and the local fixer wants to know before they find out the hard way

A civic audit has flagged a pattern of micro-transactions — fractions of a quanta, too small to notice — being skimmed from thousands of PayNode users simultaneously; someone has compromised a transit terminal network and is running an extremely patient theft
